summary: Jessie Pons is a scholar of history, archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Paris-Sorbonne University by 2011 and served as a Junior Professor at Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2019).
Jesung Woo works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Woo earned a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania and held a post at Dongguk University (attested 2001–2003).
Jey Flick works in Indology and Buddhist studies. Flick studied under Sheldon Pollock and held a post at the University of California, Berkeley.
Jian Deng works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Deng studied as a disciple under Weijue Shi and succeeded him in 2005.

Jian Ouyang (1871–1943) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Renshan Yang (around 1907–1911) and founded the China Institute of Inner Learning, serving as its head from around 1922 to 1943.

Jiang Wu specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. After graduate studies at Nankai University, Wu completed a doctorate at Harvard University under Tu Weiming and Robert M. Gimello (attested 2002), and became a professor at the University of Arizona (attested 2011–2018).
Jianming Hu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (attested 2015). Hu held a research position at Komazawa University (attested 2015).
Jiaqi Wang (1895–1959) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology. Wang studied as a disciple under Gongga Rinpoche and was a PhD student at Columbia University.

Jiayao An works in history, archaeology, and sinology. After studying under Su Bai (around 1979–1982), An held a research and laboratory director post at the Institute of Archaeology, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences from around 1982.

Jiegang Gu (1893–1980) was a sinologist and historian. He studied at Peking University under Taiyan Zhang and Hu Shih, later holding posts at Peking University, Fudan University, the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.
Jien Abe (1937–2001) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed graduate studies at the University of Tokyo (attested 1973) and served as a professor at Meiji University until 2001.

Jifu Lan is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Lan studied at Tunghai University (around 1965–1969) and was a full-time researcher at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies until retiring in 2019.

Jigdal Dagchen Sakya (1929–2016) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Ngawang Thutop Wangchuk, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and held a post at the University of Washington (around 1960–1969).

Jigme Chhoeda works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Druk Sangag Choeling and Tango monasteries under several traditional teachers, and held leadership posts at Tango Monastery, Dratshang Lhentshog, and the Central Monastic Body.
Jigme Chökyi Sengge works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.
Jigme Pema Wangchen works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Dzi Gar Khenpo Nor Yang, Drukpa Khenpo Ngawang Chödrak, and Mi-pham-bśad-sgrub-chos-kyi-ñin-byed-mchog.
Jigme Tenpai Nyima studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Jigmeth Junu is a Buddhist studies scholar. Junu completed an MA at Fo Guang University (attested 2013) supervised by Yongdong Shi, and also studied under Hui Xian.
Jikai Fujiyoshi (1915–1996) specialized in Buddhist studies. He was a member at Kyoto University (attested 1967) and served as a professor at Rissho University.

Jikido Takasaki (1926–2013) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned doctorates from Savitribai Phule Pune University and the University of Tokyo, later holding professorships at the University of Tokyo and Waseda University, and serving as president of Tsurumi Women's University.
